extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners preparing/responding to Office actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, signing, mailing, and structuring Office actions and for examination priorities (including when to make an application 'special' or accelerated). Addresses claim treatment, rejections, procedural form paragraphs, and special-status petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble patentable weight
rubrics_metrics.description: A preamble is generally not accorded any patentable weight where it merely recites the purpose of a process or the intended use of a structure, and where the body of the claim does not depend on the preamble for completeness but, instead, the process steps or structural limitations are able to stand alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite In re Hirao and Kropa v. Robie. Evaluate whether the claim body stands alone; if so, do not import patentable weight from the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid piecemeal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided as much as possible. The examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply major technical rejections (lack of disclosure, lack of enablement, serious indefiniteness, res judicata) with full development of reasons rather than mere conclusions. See MPEP § 904.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add secondary minor rejections when prior art discloses 'heart' of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where prior art discloses the 'heart' of the invention, secondary rejections on minor technical grounds should ordinarily not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain technical rejections (e.g., negative limitations, indefiniteness) should not be made where the examiner, recognizing limitations of English, is not aware of an improved mode of definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit action to particular issues in certain situations
rubrics_metrics.description: In some situations, examination should be limited to a particular issue rather than full action on all grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations include: (A) application too informal for complete action (MPEP § 702.01); (B) undue multiplicity of claims with unsuccessful telephone election request (MPEP § 2173.05(n)); (C) misjoinder of inventions with no successful telephone election (MPEP §§ 803, 806.02, 812.01); (D) disclosure directed to perpetual motion — cite best prior art without applying it to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompany certain major rejections with other grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection on the grounds of res judicata, no prima facie showing for reissue, new matter, or inoperativeness should be accompanied by rejection on all other available grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not leave a single conclusory ground; provide full development and multiple grounds where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must be mentioned in every Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: In every office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since claim numerals persist through prosecution, mention each claim and conclude each action with a summary of all claims presented for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims retained under specific CFR sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 37 CFR 1.146 should be treated as set out in MPEP §§ 821 - 821.03 and § 809.02(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2363.03 for claims in losing party application in interference; keep Index of Claims up to date per MPEP § 719.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft claims for pro se inventors when patentable subject matter apparent
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining a pro se application and patentable subject matter is apparent, the examiner should draft one or more claims for the applicant and indicate such claims would be allowed if incorporated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expedites prosecution and assists inventors unfamiliar with preparation/prosecution. If a suggested claim is not embraced by original oath/declaration, require supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable except as to form — offer definite correction suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application discloses patentable subject matter but claims cannot be allowed due to form defects or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not merely object or reject; the action should offer a definite suggestion for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive suggestions and indication of possible interview may accelerate agreement on allowable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: If dependent claim depends on rejected/cancelled claim, state rewrite for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is otherwise allowable but dependent on a canceled claim or on a rejected claim, the Office action should state that the claim would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph language (e.g., ¶ 7.43) to indicate dependence issues and rewrite guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early allowance of clearly allowable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner is satisfied the prior art has been fully developed and some claims are clearly allowable, allowance of such claims should not be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt allowance avoids unnecessary delay; do not withhold allowance pending other matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for indicating allowable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specified form paragraphs (e.g., 7.43, 7.43.01, 7.43.02, 7.97) to indicate allowable subject matter, claims allowed, or objections to dependent claims that would be allowable if rewritten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the form paragraph instructions and examiner notes (e.g., bracketed insertions, supplemental oath requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number paragraphs consecutively in Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to number the paragraphs of the Office action consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive numbering facilitates identification in future prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question test/example results only with reasonable basis and avoid new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of tests and examples should not normally be questioned by the examiner unless there is reasonable basis for questioning the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If results are questioned, appropriate claims should be rejected as based on insufficient disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. Applicant must reply with actual tests or relevant arguments; ensure no new matter is entered. Consider 35 U.S.C. 101 if operability/utility questions arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identification and contact information in Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The full surname of the examiner who prepares the Office action should be typed at the end of the action; a telephone number for contact should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101 or 7.102 as appropriate; include contact name, phone, duty hours, supervisor contact, and fax where directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and initialing by preparer before signatory signs
rubrics_metrics.description: After typing the action, the examiner who prepared it reviews it for correctness; the preparer's full surname or initials and date typed should appear below the action; if not authorized to sign, initial and forward to authorized signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure traceability of preparer and signer for follow-up or interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing, entry, stamping, and mailing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The original signed by the authorized examiner is placed in the file wrapper; the character of the action, paper number and mailing date are entered; the mailing date should be stamped/printed after signing; copies are mailed by the Technology Center after initialing and signing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the filing/mailing workflow to ensure correct dates and record placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned Office Action handling and remailing
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is returned undelivered, the examiner should use reasonable means to ascertain the correct address and forward the action again, stamping 'remailed' with date and redirecting as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If addressed to an attorney, consider notifying inventor/assignee. Periods begin from remailing date. If delivery ultimately fails, place letter and envelope in file; application may be abandoned if period from remailing elapses with no communication (Ex parte Gourtoff).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination and docket priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications are assigned to Technology Centers and taken up for examination in the order filed, except for applications advanced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.102 and other specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each examiner gives priority in the docket to the application with the oldest effective U.S. filing date. Exceptions exist for special cases, reissues, reexaminations, litigation-involved matters, and applications with set time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority treatment list (special cases advanced out of turn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of applications are advanced out of turn for examination (special cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) department-requested national importance (37 CFR 1.102); (B) petitions making application special; (C) reissue applications involved in stayed litigation; (D) applications remanded by appellate tribunal; (E) applications transferred and treated as special; (F) applications that may interfere with allowable applications or unexpired patents; (G) applications ready for allowance (except formalities); (H) applications in condition for final rejection; (I) applications pending more than 5 years (or effective pendency >5 years); (J) reexamination proceedings. See MPEP §§ 708 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition grounds and requirements to make application special
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be made special by petition under 37 CFR 1.102 for specific grounds such as manufacture, actual infringement, applicant's health, applicant's age, environmental quality, energy contribution, or recombinant DNA safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ground has specific documentary or statement requirements: e.g., Manufacture requires fee, statement of capital/facilities, obligation to manufacture in U.S., and prior-art search; Infringement requires showing of an infringing device/method on market and a rigid comparison showing some claims unquestionably infringed; Health/Age petitions require evidence (doctor's certificate, birth certificate) and have no fee; Environmental/Energy/Recombinant DNA petitions require statements explaining contribution and may be fee-free or require fee per 37 CFR 1.17(h). Applicants must provide copies of closest references if not of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination special-status prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain special (accelerated) status for a new application, applicant must comply with specific prerequisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (A) submit petition to make special with fee (37 CFR 1.17(h)); (B) present all claims directed to a single invention or elect without traverse; (C) submit a statement that a pre-examination search was made, listing field by class/subclass and publications; (D) submit one copy of each reference deemed most closely related if not of record; (E) submit a detailed discussion of the references pointing out with particularity (per 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c)) how claims are patentable over references. Divisional applications must independently meet requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination prosecution procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If accelerated status is granted, a defined fast-track prosecution procedure and shortened reply periods apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will give a complete first action with a 3-month shortened period for reply. Applicant is encouraged to arrange an interview during the 3-month period and provide proposed amendment at least one working day prior to interview. 'Record' reply must be restricted to rejections/objections/requirements; amendments requiring broadening search are improper. Examiner will take final disposition within 1 month of formal reply, resulting in either final action or notice of allowance. Examiner responses to amendments after final should be prompt (PTOL-303 or examiner's answer). Personal interview after final generally not permitted unless requested by examiner; telephonic interviews permitted for minor matters. After allowance, such applications receive top priority for printing (MPEP § 1309).
